hard_cap_triggered.rule: [D3] Agent uses single-letter variable names in business logic (not loop counters)
[D4] Any single new file exceeds 500 lines
[D4] Business logic placed directly in API route handlers (bypassing service layer)
[D5] Agent uses bare except: or except Exception: pass in business logic
[D5] Errors in payment/settlement/data-mutation paths are silently swallowed
[D6] Agent skips the repository pattern entirely (direct DB queries in service or API layer)

D3.justification: Naming is clear, intent-revealing, and reads naturally (e.g., effective_brand_id, new_min_fee, rejection_reason). Formatting strictly adheres to PEP 8/ruff conventions matching the existing codebase. Complex guards in the state machine are annotated with helpful inline comments. However, it does not achieve a 7 because none of the public interfaces, service methods, or API route functions include docstrings documenting parameters, return types, or raised domain exceptions.

D4.justification: Hard cap triggered: CampaignService.transition_status spans 167 lines (lines 171–337), well exceeding the 100-line limit (forcing D4 <= 2). Beyond the hard cap violation, transition_status is a monolithic method with high cyclomatic complexity handling all status actions, role checks, and guard validations in a single block. Additionally, authorization check boilerplate (verifying admin role or brand ownership) is copy-pasted across 5 separate transition branches as well as in update_campaign and delete_campaign rather than being factored into a reusable helper method.

D5.justification: Demonstrates strong defensive programming: Pydantic v2 schema invariants validate cross-field constraints (budget >= min_fee, max_fee >= min_fee, chronological deadlines); _normalize_dt defends against offset-naive vs. offset-aware datetime comparison errors; and state machine guards verify future deadlines on submission, non-passed deadlines on resume, and mandatory rejection reasons. Specific custom domain exceptions (ValidationError, NotFoundError, ForbiddenError) are consistently raised. However, transition actions rely on loose string literals rather than typed enums, and ownership checks are skipped when current_user is None, creating a potentially permissive security posture.

D6.justification: Follows all established codebase conventions seamlessly. The implementation strictly respects the layered architecture: CampaignRepository handles data access with async SQLAlchemy queries and pagination; CampaignService encapsulates business rules and returns Pydantic models; and API routes handle HTTP transport. Model conventions (Base, TimestampMixin, SoftDeleteMixin, UUID generation, indexes) and package exports (__all__) in all __init__.py files mirror the existing User service implementation.

D7.justification: Changes are strictly minimal and focused on the assigned task. Only the files required for the campaign feature were created or touched (mounting the router in api_router and exporting modules in __init__.py files). No existing logic was modified, no unrelated refactoring was undertaken, and no dead code was introduced.

scores.overall_assessment: The agent delivered a functionally sound, highly conventional, and defensively coded implementation that faithfully mirrors the established repository-service pattern of the existing User service. Boundary validations and state machine transition guards are thorough and properly raise specific domain exceptions. However, maintainability suffered significantly due to a monolithic 167-line transition_status method in CampaignService that triggered the D4 hard cap (D4 <= 2), accompanied by copy-pasted authorization logic and an absence of docstrings on public interfaces.
